source.author: cic
source.text: qua re tibicen Antigenidas dixerit discipulo sane frigenti ad populum: Mihi cane et Musis; ego huic Bruto dicenti, ut solet, apud multitudinem, Mihi cane et populo, mi Brute, dixerim, ut qui audient quid efficiatur, ego etiam cur id efficiatur intellegam.
source.text_original: qua re tibicen Antigenidas dixerit discipulo sane frigenti ad populum: Mihi cane et Musis; ego huic Bruto dicenti, ut solet, apud multitudinem, Mihi cane et populo, mi Brute, dixerim, ut qui audient quid efficiatur, ego etiam cur id efficiatur intellegam.
source.text_english: For this reason the flute-player Antigenidas would say to a very dull pupil, in the presence of the public, Play for me and the Muses; and I, to this Brutus speaking, as he usually does, before the crowd, Play for me and the people, my dear Brutus, would say it, so that those who are listening may understand what is being achieved, and I too may understand why it is being achieved.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: nec mirum, si me et absentem et iam diu absque usu Latinae linguae semibarbarumque homo Latinissimus et facundissimus superet, cum praesentem Iouinianum Iesu bone, qualem et quantum uirum, cuius nemo scripta intellegeret, qui sibi tantum caneret et Musis! eloquentiae suae mole oppresserit.
reuse.text_original: nec mirum, si me et absentem et iam diu absque usu Latinae linguae semibarbarumque homo Latinissimus et facundissimus superet, cum praesentem Iouinianum — Iesu bone, qualem et quantum uirum, cuius nemo scripta intellegeret, qui sibi tantum caneret et Musis! — eloquentiae suae mole oppresserit.
reuse.text_english: Nor is it surprising if he surpasses me, both absent and long since out of practice in the Latin language and a half-barbarian, being a most Latin and eloquent man, when he has overwhelmed the present Jovinian, good Jesus, what a man and how great a man he is, whose writings no one would understand, who would sing only to himself and to the Muses, by the weight of his own eloquence.
